Assume the standard scalar field is \(\mathbb{R}\), and “dimension” means algebraic (Hamel) dimension.

Let

\[
V=\{f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}\}
\]

with pointwise addition and scalar multiplication. Write

\[
\mathfrak{c}=|\mathbb{R}|=2^{\aleph_0}.
\]

### Step 1: Count the number of functions in \(V\)

The set \(V\) is exactly \(\mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{R}}\), so

\[
|V|=|\mathbb{R}|^{|\mathbb{R}|}=\mathfrak{c}^{\mathfrak{c}}.
\]

Since \(\mathfrak{c}=2^{\aleph_0}\),

\[
\mathfrak{c}^{\mathfrak{c}}
=(2^{\aleph_0})^{2^{\aleph_0}}
=2^{\aleph_0\cdot 2^{\aleph_0}}
=2^{2^{\aleph_0}}
=2^{\mathfrak{c}}.
\]

Thus

\[
|V|=2^{\mathfrak{c}}.
\]

### Step 2: Relate the cardinality of a vector space to its dimension

Let \(d=\dim_{\mathbb{R}} V\), and let \(\mathcal{B}\) be a Hamel basis of \(V\). Then \(|\mathcal{B}|=d\).

Every element of \(V\) is a finite linear combination of basis elements:

\[
f=\sum_{i=1}^{n} a_i b_i,
\]

where \(a_i\in\mathbb{R}\) and \(b_i\in\mathcal{B}\). Therefore the number of possible vectors is at most the number of finite choices of basis elements together with real coefficients:

\[
|V|\le \max(\mathfrak{c},d).
\]

Also, since \(\mathcal{B}\subseteq V\),

\[
d\le |V|=2^{\mathfrak{c}}.
\]

So

\[
2^{\mathfrak{c}}=|V|\le \max(\mathfrak{c},d)\le 2^{\mathfrak{c}}.
\]

Hence

\[
\max(\mathfrak{c},d)=2^{\mathfrak{c}}.
\]

But by Cantor’s theorem,

\[
\mathfrak{c}<2^{\mathfrak{c}}.
\]

Therefore the maximum can equal \(2^{\mathfrak{c}}\) only if

\[
d=2^{\mathfrak{c}}.
\]

Thus

\[
\dim_{\mathbb{R}} V=2^{\mathfrak{c}}=2^{2^{\aleph_0}}.
\]

\[
\boxed{2^{2^{\aleph_0}}}
\]
